On Oct 21, PHP shipped fixes for two critical flaws now called PHP2Shell. The NSA put out an advisory the same morning.

If your store runs on PHP (Magento, Adobe Commerce, WooCommerce, Shopware), this is the short version.

1. The bug is in PHP itself, not in your plugins. Updating plugins doesn't fix it.
2. The fixed versions are 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12. Ask your host which one your store runs on, and get the answer in writing.
3. A follow-up flaw was disclosed on Oct 23. Ask again next week.
4. After any patch, place a test order on your phone. A fix that quietly breaks checkout costs more than the bug did so far.

Sansec, which tracks card skimming on stores, says it hasn't seen skimming from this yet.

\[If engineering confirms: one line on whether Tagada's checkout was affected, and when it was patched.\]

When did you last ask your host which version of PHP your store runs on?

So more ads are being shown, and each one costs more than it did a year ago.

You can't change Meta's price. You can change what a click is worth once it reaches your store.

Two numbers worth pulling from last month before you raise budgets:

1. Out of every 100 paid visitors who reached your checkout, how many paid?
2. What did the average order add after the payment? An add-on, a second unit, a subscription.

Move both, and a dearer click can still cost you less per order.

On Oct 21 the OCC finalized its rule for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act. It takes effect Jan 18, 2027.

What it says, in plain words:
- An issuer has to hold reserves at least equal to the stablecoins it has out.
- Redemptions generally get paid within two business days.
- Issuers still can't pay interest just for holding a stablecoin.

None of this means you should add stablecoins to your checkout next week.

It does mean the dollar coins some of your customers already hold now come with written federal rules on reserves and redemption. That's usually the point where more stores start asking the question.

The Visa and Mastercard swipe-fee settlement goes to a final approval hearing on Nov 16.

What it would change, per Payments Dive (Oct 16):
- Credit interchange down 10 basis points for five years.
- A 1.25% rate on standard consumer cards for eight years.
- The right to decline some premium and commercial credit cards.
- New rights to add surcharges or offer discounts, to steer customers toward cheaper cards.

For scale: merchants paid 2.35% on average on Visa and Mastercard transactions in 2024 (Nilson Report).

Walmart, the NRF and RILA have objected, so none of this is final yet.

One thing worth doing before the ruling: pull last month's orders and split them by card type. Standard, premium, commercial. That split tells you whether any of this moves the needle for your store.

\[If confirmed: where that card-type split lives in the TagadaPay dashboard.\]

Meta now lets you book an ad burst: your reach packed into a window of 3 to 24 hours (Ads Super Burst). It's also testing First Impression Ads in the US, the first ad slot in Feed, one brand per day.

Both sell the same thing. A lot of people at your checkout at the same time.

The ad dashboard stops at the tap. What happens after it is on you.

Before you book a window:
1. Place a test order on your phone, on mobile data, through the exact link the ad will use.
2. Count the fields between the cart and the pay button.
3. Try a card that declines. See what the customer sees, and whether there's another way to pay on the same page.
4. Check that your post-purchase offer loads after the payment, not before it.

Then book the window.
